#!/usr/bin/env bash
# shellcheck enable=all

set -o errexit -o nounset -o pipefail

export PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin

if [[ "${OSTYPE}" == "darwin"* ]]; then

bsv_root="$(realpath "$(dirname "$(realpath -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")"/..)"
readonly bsv_root

if [[ "${OSTYPE}" == "darwin"* ]]; then
  ln --symbolic --force /nix "${bsv_root}"/nix
fi

mkdir --parents "${bsv_root}"/nix/store

deno="${bsv_root}"/bin/deno

export DENO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1
export DENO_DIR="${bsv_root}"/tmp/deno

export http_proxy=http://10.0.1.18:3128
export https_proxy=http://10.0.1.18:3128
export no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost,andestech.com

exec "${deno}" run --allow-all --unstable-ffi "${bsv_root}/src/cli/mod.ts" "$@"

# Building Packages

Once inside the BSV environment, build packages with `bsv build` command:

```console
(bsv) $ bsv build <installable>...
```

## Installable

An [installable](https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.31/command-ref/new-cli/nix#installables) is something that can be built and added to the Nix store.

The most common type of installable is by specifying a flake output attribute, in the form of `flakeref#attrpath`.

## Listing Packages

BSV provides a convenience command to list all packages in a flake:

```console
(bsv) $ bsv list-derivations
<!-- cmdrun bsv list-derivations /bsv#legacyPackages.x86_64-linux.x86_64-linux-gnu | head -n10; echo ... -->
```

In BSV, packages are organized in a hierarchical tree structure where attribute paths use `.` as the separator between each segment.

## Build a Package

Start by building a simple package, such as `binutils` in the `/bsv` flake:

```console
(bsv) $ bsv build /bsv#binutils
<!-- cmdrun bsv build /bsv#binutils | tail -n1 -->
```

~~~admonish note
More often than not, this command will not actually build the `binutils` package locally.
It will download a pre-built version from BSV's cache server instead, if the package has already been built by the CI server.
~~~

The command will output the path of `binutils` in the Nix store.
To verify the build result, inspect the content of the `binutils` package:

```console
(bsv) $ ls "$(bsv build /bsv#binutils)"
<!-- cmdrun ls "$(bsv build /bsv#binutils)" -->
(bsv) $ "$(bsv build /bsv#binutils)"/usr/local/bin/as --version
<!-- cmdrun "$(bsv build /bsv#binutils)"/usr/local/bin/as --version | head -n1 -->
```

~~~admonish note
The packages are only accessible via `/nix/store/...` inside the BSV environment, which mounts the Nix store used by BSV at `/nix`.

To reference the Nix store outside the BSV environment, you need to prefix it with the path to the BSV installation, e.g., `/path/to/bsv/nix/store/...`.
~~~

1	# BSV Environment
2	
3	BSV uses the BSV environment to normalize differences between host systems, providing a consistent execution environment for its commands.
4	
5	BSV is designed so that most commands only work when executed inside the BSV environment.
6	
7	## Characteristics
8	
9	### Uniform Paths
10	
11	The BSV environment mounts the BSV repository at `/bsv`, and then mounts `/bsv/nix` at `/nix`.
12	This ensures that BSV can reference the BSV repository and the Nix store under the same paths, regardless of where the BSV repository was checked out.
13	
14	### Consistent Tooling
15	
16	Programs used by BSV may not be installed on the host system, or may have outdated or incompatible versions.
17	
18	BSV resolves this by bundling all necessary dependencies and configuring them to use internal settings defined by BSV to ensure consistent behavior.
19	
20	### Isolation
21	
22	Each BSV installation operates independently with minimal interaction with the host system or other BSV installations.
23	
24	## Activation
25	
26	To enter the BSV environment, run the command inside the BSV repository:
27	
28	```console
29	$ ./bin/bsv env
30	(bsv) $
31	```
32

# BSV Environment

BSV uses the BSV environment to normalize differences between host systems, providing a consistent execution environment for its commands.

BSV is designed so that most commands only work when executed inside the BSV environment.

## Characteristics

### Uniform Paths

The BSV environment mounts the BSV repository at `/bsv`, and then mounts `/bsv/nix` at `/nix`.
This ensures that BSV can reference the BSV repository and the Nix store under the same paths, regardless of where the BSV repository was checked out.

### Consistent Tooling

Programs used by BSV may not be installed on the host system, or may have outdated or incompatible versions.

BSV resolves this by bundling all necessary dependencies and configuring them to use internal settings defined by BSV to ensure consistent behavior.

### Isolation

Each BSV installation operates independently with minimal interaction with the host system or other BSV installations.

## Activation

To enter the BSV environment, run the command inside the BSV repository:

```console
$ ./bin/bsv env
(bsv) $
```

This will launch a `bash` sub-shell with `(bsv)` prepended to the prompt.

The following chapters assume that commands are executed within this environment.

# Contributing

## Initialize the development environment

Install development tools (formatters, linters, etc) to work on BSV by running:

```
(bsv) $ bsv init-dev
<!-- cmdrun bsv init-dev >& /dev/null -->
```

## Code Formatting

BSV enforces a strict code-formatting style:
- Nix: [nixfmt-tree](https://github.com/NixOS/nixfmt)
- Deno: [Deno's built-in formatter](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/fundamentals/linting_and_formatting/#formatting)

To automatically format the codebase according to the coding style, run the following command:

```
(bsv) $ bsv fmt
<!-- cmdrun bsv fmt 2>&1 | head -n5 -->
```

## Checking and Linting

Before committing, verify that the codebase passes all linting and static checks:

```
(bsv) $ bsv check
<!-- cmdrun bsv check 2>&1 | head -n5 -->
```

This runs:
- Type checking (`deno check`) and linting (`deno lint`) on Deno/TypeScript files.
- Linting (`nixf-diagnose`) on Nix sources.
- Check if the BSV flake can be successfully evaluated.
- Packages conform to the naming standard and use allowed builders.

## Commit Style

Each commit should represent a single, coherent change.

Format the subject line of a commit message in the style:

```
<scope>: <summary>
```

The `scope` can be either `bsv` (tree-wide changes), a specific component (e.g. `ci`, `report`) or a package/test (e.g. `pkgs/andes/gcc-stage2`).

The `summary` should be a short imperative (a sentence starting with a verb).
For consistency, the first word of the sentence is not capitalized.

## Submitting Changes

To submit changes to BSV, fork the main `RD-SW/bsv` repository and open a pull request.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

Build System V (BSV) is a Nix-powered build system that produces Andes RISC-V toolchains, packages, and test results. Package recipes are written in Nix (`pkgs/`, `lib/`, `tests/`, `reports/`); the `bsv` CLI and the CI/report web servers are written in TypeScript on Deno (`src/`).

## The BSV environment (read this first)

Almost every command runs in two layers:

```console
$ ./bin/bsv init          # one-time setup; downloads prebuilt nix/deno/bwrap
$ ./bin/bsv env           # enter a bash sub-shell, prompt becomes "(bsv) $"
(bsv) $ bsv build /bsv#binutils
```

- `./bin/bsv` is the real entry point. The top-level `./bsv` is deprecated.
- The environment mounts the repo at `/bsv` and its Nix store at `/nix`, so paths are identical no matter where the repo is checked out. Always reference flakes/packages as `/bsv#...`, not relative paths.
- Commands with `requiresBsvEnv = true` (build, check, fmt, log, eval, repl, gc, delete, list-derivations, build-shell, verify-reproducibility, gen-hash, init-dev) fail unless run inside `bsv env`. `init`, `env`, `list-commands`, `help` do not.
- Outside the environment, a store path `/nix/store/...` must be prefixed with the repo root (e.g. `/local/nick/bsv/nix/store/...`).
- The env hardcodes a corporate proxy (`http://10.0.1.18:3128`) and the binary cache `https://atcbsv.andestech.com/cache`.

## Common commands (run inside `bsv env`)

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `bsv build <installable>...` | Build derivations; prints the output store path. Pulls from the cache if CI already built it. |
| `bsv list-derivations [flakeref#attrpath]` | List every buildable attribute path (default `/bsv#legacyPackages`). |
| `bsv log <installable>` | Print a build log (local, then falls back to the binary cache). |
| `bsv build-shell <derivation>` | Enter the bwrap sandbox for a derivation to debug a build. `--extra-tools` adds gdb/strace/vim; `--command`, `--bind`, `--env` available. |
| `bsv verify-reproducibility <derivation>` | Rebuild and diff outputs; runs diffoscope on mismatch. |
| `bsv eval <args>` / `bsv repl` | `nix eval` / `nix repl` against `/bsv/flake.nix`. |
| `bsv gen-hash` | Read a `url = "...";` line from stdin, print it plus the SRI `hash = "...";`. |
| `bsv delete <installable>` / `bsv delete --all` | Remove store objects (and their referrer closure). |
| `bsv gc` | Garbage-collect the store. |
| `bsv list-commands` | List all subcommands. Add `--help` to any command for its options. |

### Installables

An installable is `flakeref#attrpath`, e.g. `/bsv#binutils` or `/bsv#andes.nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d`. Attribute paths are a hierarchical tree with `.` separators (e.g. `/bsv#x86_64-linux-gnu.tests.bs3.supertest.nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d.gcc.O2.qemu`). Use `bsv list-derivations` to discover valid paths.

## Lint, format, check (this repo's equivalent of "run the tests")

```console
(bsv) $ bsv init-dev   # one-time: build nixd, nixf-diagnose, nixfmt-tree
(bsv) $ bsv check      # type-check + lint TS, lint Nix, eval the flake, verify naming/builders
(bsv) $ bsv fmt        # format all Nix (nixfmt-tree) and TS (deno fmt)
```

`bsv check` is what CI (`.gitea/workflows/check.yaml`) runs, plus a `bsv fmt` diff to enforce formatting. It checks four Deno configs: the root `deno.jsonc` (`src/`) and `src/{ci,report,utils}/webui/deno.json`. There is no separate unit-test suite for the CLI; correctness is enforced by type-checking, lint, and flake evaluation.

To type-check or lint a single TS file directly: `deno check --config deno.jsonc src/cli/commands/build.ts` (use the matching `webui/deno.json` for files under those dirs).

## Running package/toolchain tests

Tests are Nix derivations under `tests/`, surfaced in the attribute tree (e.g. `x86_64-linux-gnu.tests.hello.c.<toolchain>...`, `...tests.bs3.supertest...`). **Building a test runs it** - the builder compiles the program and executes it under QEMU/SID inside the sandbox, and the build fails if the test fails. So you run one test by building its installable:

```console
(bsv) $ bsv build /bsv#x86_64-linux-gnu.tests.hello.c.nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d.<arch>.gcc.<flags>.qemu
```

`reports/*.nix` define which test derivations get aggregated into the build report tables (the source of truth for the CI matrix). To run RISC-V ELF binaries through Andes QEMU outside a derivation, use the `qemu-runner` agent (it handles a semihosting fd-9 quirk).

## Repository layout

- `src/cli/` - the `bsv` CLI. `commands.ts` registers subcommands; each `commands/<name>.ts` exports `default` (handler), `help`, and `requiresBsvEnv`. `mod.ts` sets up the env and dispatches.
- `src/utils/` - shared TS helpers (`run.ts`, `nix/`, `parse_args.ts`, `console.ts`, etc.). `src/ci/` and `src/report/` are Oak web servers (run via their shebang `deno run`).
- `lib/` - Nix library: builders (`bwrap-derivation.nix`, `configure-make.nix`, `cmake-builder.nix`, ...), fetchers, and helpers like `mapDependentCartesianProduct` (used to generate the test matrix). Entry point `lib/default.nix`.
- `pkgs/` - one directory per package; `default.nix` is the recipe. `pkgs/<system>.nix` and `pkgs/x86_64-windows/` assemble the per-system package set. `pkgs/andes/` holds the Andes toolchain components.
- `builders/` - the small set of allowed Nix builders (`bwrap-builder@v0`, `extract-tarball@v0`, `fetch-git@v0`, etc.); `bsv check` rejects any derivation using a builder outside this set.
- `tests/`, `reports/` - test recipes and their report aggregation; `*-map.nix` files map toolchains to arch flags, compiler flags, and QEMU runners.
- `default.nix` / `flake.nix` - flake outputs: `legacyPackages.<system>`, `checks`, `apps` (qemu/sid runners, nix tooling), `reports`, `mirror`.
- `docs/` - mdBook user documentation (`docs/src/*.md`).

### Package recipe shape

A recipe is a function taking `{ bsv, build, host ? build }` and returning a derivation built with `bsv.lib.bwrapDerivation` (or another `lib` builder). It sets `name`, `root` (the build deps), `env` (including `src` from `lib.fetchTarball`/`lib.fetchGit`), `builder` (e.g. `lib.configureMake { ... }`), and `system`. See `pkgs/hello/default.nix` for the canonical minimal example.

### Toolchain naming

Toolchain triples follow `nds{32,64}le-{elf,linux}-{newlib,mculib,glibc,musl}-v5[fde]`, e.g. `nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d`. The full list lives in `reports/tests.nix` and `tests/*/default.nix`.

## Conventions

- Commit subject: `<scope>: <summary>`. Scope is `bsv` (tree-wide), a component (`ci`, `report`), or a package/test path (`pkgs/andes/gcc-stage2`). Summary is a lowercase imperative sentence.
- New packages must be named to match their attribute path and use only the allowed builders, or `bsv check` fails.

```

- `./bin/bsv` is the real entry point. The top-level `./bsv` is deprecated.
- The environment mounts the repo at `/bsv` and its Nix store at `/nix`, so paths are identical no matter where the repo is checked out. Always reference flakes/packages as `/bsv#...`, not relative paths.
- Commands with `requiresBsvEnv = true` (build, check, fmt, log, eval, repl, gc, delete, list-derivations, build-shell, verify-reproducibility, gen-hash, init-dev) fail unless run inside `bsv env`. `init`, `env`, `list-commands`, `help` do not.
- Outside the environment, a store path `/nix/store/...` must be prefixed with the repo root (e.g. `/local/nick/bsv/nix/store/...`).
- The env hardcodes a corporate proxy (`http://10.0.1.18:3128`) and the binary cache `https://atcbsv.andestech.com/cache`.

## Common commands (run inside `bsv env`)

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `bsv build <installable>...` | Build derivations; prints the output store path. Pulls from the cache if CI already built it. |
| `bsv list-derivations [flakeref#attrpath]` | List every buildable attribute path (default `/bsv#legacyPackages`). |
| `bsv log <installable>` | Print a build log (local, then falls back to the binary cache). |
| `bsv build-shell <derivation>` | Enter the bwrap sandbox for a derivation to debug a build. `--extra-tools` adds gdb/strace/vim; `--command`, `--bind`, `--env` available. |
| `bsv verify-reproducibility <derivation>` | Rebuild and diff outputs; runs diffoscope on mismatch. |
| `bsv eval <args>` / `bsv repl` | `nix eval` / `nix repl` against `/bsv/flake.nix`. |
| `bsv gen-hash` | Read a `url = "...";` line from stdin, print it plus the SRI `hash = "...";`. |
| `bsv delete <installable>` / `bsv delete --all` | Remove store objects (and their referrer closure). |
| `bsv gc` | Garbage-collect the store. |
| `bsv list-commands` | List all subcommands. Add `--help` to any command for its options. |

### Installables

An installable is `flakeref#attrpath`, e.g. `/bsv#binutils` or `/bsv#andes.nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d`. Attribute paths are a hierarchical tree with `.` separators (e.g. `/bsv#x86_64-linux-gnu.tests.bs3.supertest.nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d.gcc.O2.qemu`). Use `bsv list-derivations` to discover valid paths.

## Lint, format, check (this repo's equivalent of "run the tests")

```console
(bsv) $ bsv init-dev   # one-time: build nixd, nixf-diagnose, nixfmt-tree
(bsv) $ bsv check      # type-check + lint TS, lint Nix, eval the flake, verify naming/builders
(bsv) $ bsv fmt        # format all Nix (nixfmt-tree) and TS (deno fmt)
```

`bsv check` is what CI (`.gitea/workflows/check.yaml`) runs, plus a `bsv fmt` diff to enforce formatting. It checks four Deno configs: the root `deno.jsonc` (`src/`) and `src/{ci,report,utils}/webui/deno.json`. There is no separate unit-test suite for the CLI; correctness is enforced by type-checking, lint, and flake evaluation.

To type-check or lint a single TS file directly: `deno check --config deno.jsonc src/cli/commands/build.ts` (use the matching `webui/deno.json` for files under those dirs).

## Running package/toolchain tests

Tests are Nix derivations under `tests/`, surfaced in the attribute tree (e.g. `x86_64-linux-gnu.tests.hello.c.<toolchain>...`, `...tests.bs3.supertest...`). **Building a test runs it** - the builder compiles the program and executes it under QEMU/SID inside the sandbox, and the build fails if the test fails. So you run one test by building its installable:

```console
(bsv) $ bsv build /bsv#x86_64-linux-gnu.tests.hello.c.nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d.<arch>.gcc.<flags>.qemu
```

`reports/*.nix` define which test derivations get aggregated into the build report tables (the source of truth for the CI matrix). To run RISC-V ELF binaries through Andes QEMU outside a derivation, use the `qemu-runner` agent (it handles a semihosting fd-9 quirk).

## Repository layout

- `src/cli/` - the `bsv` CLI. `commands.ts` registers subcommands; each `commands/<name>.ts` exports `default` (handler), `help`, and `requiresBsvEnv`. `mod.ts` sets up the env and dispatches.
- `src/utils/` - shared TS helpers (`run.ts`, `nix/`, `parse_args.ts`, `console.ts`, etc.). `src/ci/` and `src/report/` are Oak web servers (run via their shebang `deno run`).
- `lib/` - Nix library: builders (`bwrap-derivation.nix`, `configure-make.nix`, `cmake-builder.nix`, ...), fetchers, and helpers like `mapDependentCartesianProduct` (used to generate the test matrix). Entry point `lib/default.nix`.
- `pkgs/` - one directory per package; `default.nix` is the recipe. `pkgs/<system>.nix` and `pkgs/x86_64-windows/` assemble the per-system package set. `pkgs/andes/` holds the Andes toolchain components.
- `builders/` - the small set of allowed Nix builders (`bwrap-builder@v0`, `extract-tarball@v0`, `fetch-git@v0`, etc.); `bsv check` rejects any derivation using a builder outside this set.
- `tests/`, `reports/` - test recipes and their report aggregation; `*-map.nix` files map toolchains to arch flags, compiler flags, and QEMU runners.
- `default.nix` / `flake.nix` - flake outputs: `legacyPackages.<system>`, `checks`, `apps` (qemu/sid runners, nix tooling), `reports`, `mirror`.
- `docs/` - mdBook user documentation (`docs/src/*.md`).

### Package recipe shape

A recipe is a function taking `{ bsv, build, host ? build }` and returning a derivation built with `bsv.lib.bwrapDerivation` (or another `lib` builder). It sets `name`, `root` (the build deps), `env` (including `src` from `lib.fetchTarball`/`lib.fetchGit`), `builder` (e.g. `lib.configureMake { ... }`), and `system`. See `pkgs/hello/default.nix` for the canonical minimal example.

### Toolchain naming

Toolchain triples follow `nds{32,64}le-{elf,linux}-{newlib,mculib,glibc,musl}-v5[fde]`, e.g. `nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d`. The full list lives in `reports/tests.nix` and `tests/*/default.nix`.

## Conventions

- Commit subject: `<scope>: <summary>`. Scope is `bsv` (tree-wide), a component (`ci`, `report`), or a package/test path (`pkgs/andes/gcc-stage2`). Summary is a lowercase imperative sentence.
- New packages must be named to match their attribute path and use only the allowed builders, or `bsv check` fails.
